spec.title: Offered load (all attempts/s) vs original rate (new events/s)
spec.description: attempts = every HTTP request k6 sends (first tries + retries); new events = iterations started (the original rate). With retries the attempts line should rise ABOVE the new-events line during the slow part. Look at whether it comes back down after the toxic is removed (zoom to events.tsv). Surprising: attempts staying high long after removal (self-sustaining), or no rise at all. k6 series are not marked stale after a run, last values can linger. Metric k6_b9_attempts_total is ADDED BY B9.

spec.title: Goodput: events accepted (202) per second
spec.description: Iterations that ended with a 202, per variant. Should equal the original rate while healthy, fall during the slow part, and come back after removal. Surprising: staying near zero long after removal (metastable) or exceeding the original rate for a moment (backlog draining). Metric k6_b9_unique_ok_total is ADDED BY B9.

spec.title: Share of attempts answered 202
spec.description: 202 answers divided by attempts. Healthy = 100%. Recovery in the analysis means this is at least 99% (and attempts/s within 10% of the original) for 10 s. Surprising: a plateau below 100% after the toxic is gone. Uses k6_b9_resp_202_total and k6_b9_attempts_total (ADDED BY B9).

spec.title: Retries and give-ups per second
spec.description: Retries = attempts after the first try. Give-ups = iterations that used all tries without a 202. In the immediate variant retries should be several times the original rate during the slow part. Metrics k6_b9_retries_total and k6_b9_giveups_total are ADDED BY B9.

spec.title: Answers by kind (client side)
spec.description: 202 = accepted, 503 = server said no (pool wait over 2 s), other = mostly status 0, the 1 s client timeout (the client gave up before the server answered). Many 'other' means the client leaves while the request still waits in the server queue. Metrics k6_b9_resp_* are ADDED BY B9.

spec.title: Wasted work: Postgres commits vs 202s the client saw
spec.description: Commits per second in Postgres (includes the small warm-up/self-check traffic only outside the run) against 202 answers per second at the client. Commits above 202s = the database stored events whose client had already given up (or whose 202 arrived late). Surprising: commits high while goodput is low = capacity spent on work nobody uses.

spec.title: Pool: in use and waiting
spec.description: In use = total - idle connections (max 5 here). Waiting = requests queued for a connection. A waiting queue of hundreds that does not shrink after removal is the stuck state. Surprising: waiting stays high with the pool full while the database is already fast again.

spec.title: Pool wait time p50 / p99
spec.description: Time a request waits for a connection. The server gives up at 2 s (PG_CONN_TIMEOUT_MS), the client at 1 s. p50 above 1 s means most served requests are already abandoned by the client. Surprising: p99 pinned at 2 s after removal.

spec.title: Server errors by type
spec.description: ep_db_errors_by_type_total: pool_timeout (waited longer than 2 s for a connection) and statement_timeout. Surprising: errors of other types.

spec.title: Requests in flight (server) and k6 VUs
spec.description: In flight = requests the server has accepted and not answered. k6 VUs = virtual users busy (an iteration holds its VU while it retries). Both rising together is the queue growing. Surprising: VUs reaching the max (8000) means invalid run.

spec.title: Attempt latency p50 / p99 (client view)
spec.description: k6_http_req_duration_seconds is a native histogram. The client timeout is 1 s, so p99 should flatten near 1 s while the system is overloaded. Surprising: p99 well above 1 s (timeout not working) or back to a few ms right after removal.

spec.title: CPU busy by pinned group
spec.description: Server (cpus 0,6), Postgres (1,7,2,8), k6 (3,9,4,10) from node_exporter. Rejecting and timing-out requests still costs the server CPU. Surprising: server near 100% (the node process, not the database, is the limit).

spec.title: Node process CPU and memory
spec.description: CPU seconds per second of the ingest-api process (1.0 = one core) and its resident memory in GB. Memory growing means many queued requests are held. Surprising: memory still growing after removal.

spec.title: k6 dropped iterations
spec.description: Must be 0. Above 0 = k6 ran out of VUs and did not start all planned new events: the run is discarded (retries hold VUs).

spec.title: k6 CPU headroom
spec.description: Busy share of the k6 cpus. Keep under about 70%. Above that the generator, not the server, may be limiting.

spec.title: Event loop lag
spec.description: nodejs_eventloop_lag_seconds of the server. Large lag means the single Node thread is saturated (so the limit is the server CPU, not the pool). Surprising: lag above 100 ms in the healthy part.

spec.title: 1. The verdict: did the offered load rise, and did the system come back?
2. The mechanism: queues, timeouts, wasted work
